text_fidelity_a:
Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count After 40-some years on the technical side of electrochemical fabrication (12" wafer fab) and manufacturing that included the IBM PS1 & PS2 birth … cleanliness is Godliness. I've likely tried every chemical variant of cleaner ever invented, though many fewer are now permitted for USA use.

Though impractical for the laptop, some excellent cleaners in the $1000/gal category might be suggested for cleansing strategic missile-related monitors and surfaces. The value and reliability of what device you are cleaning is the most critical consideration when choosing a cleaner. A wrong choice might pay back immediately with bad results, dissolving the anti-reflective coating or lamination of the touch screen overlay, removing specialized keyboard paints, ruining distinctive finishes, etc. For another, that same choice might do a bang-up job on the big screen at home, but when used on a laptop, it slowly dissolves and/or corrodes critical interconnects as you pass through dewpoints on that 17-hour airplane ride to Sydney.

Q: What is the best cleaner to shine on my $1500 laptop?

A: Not the cheapest $4/qt cleaner. Not one of grandma's window elixirs.

Behind the scenes, there is likely no other technical discussion as critical as cleaning and cleaners. Billions are spent every year on the problem. What I know from experience is that an alcohol solvent-based cleaner does a pretty good job erasing the symbology that makes my lighted keyboard legible. I look for a cleaner to remove the latent crusty-goo residue left by that anti-viral covid computer cleaner six months ago. Some cleaners with notionally benign saponifiers that sell under the enviro-friendly, "Green!", "non-GMO!" moniker is known to corrode solder joints and electro-plating to short the keyboard and LCD/OLED out.

Finding the right balance between solvent and saponifiers has not evolved smoothly. Saponifiers remove organics. The stuff that sprays out of your mouth and nose when yelling at the laptop. Solvents remove inorganics like hand cream, french fry grease, and Cheeto dust. I've rolled up all of this wisdom in my 'Rule #446 - Do not buy the cheapest electronics cleaner. Ever.'

This Monster cleaner is not cheap. It's a premium cleaner under a known premium brand. Given Monster brands, cleaning processes are the #1 priority for their established long-lived high-fidelity interconnection. My laptop has a touch screen that demands a non-delaminating cleaner and a lighted keyboard with that funky paint and laser-etched symbology. This Monster cleaner did an unexpectedly quick, no-smudge job on the laptop. All is good.
text_fidelity_b: Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 2nd) I just received my kindle fire today. I had a hard time deciding between the HD, this, and the paperwhite. I decided on this one, because I really thought I'd like the immersion reading. I have an audible account and I've been reading along to the audiobooks. It's amazing how fast I can get through the books (at 3x speed) and I really retain the info. The immersion reading is super-easy to use and definitely worth upgrading to this. The whole point of the kindle is to read more, and this new feature makes it possible to read 2 or 3 times as many books in the same amount of time. I'm an average-speed reader and was able to read 4 books (with the help of the audiobook reading pace) in the last 30 days and one was the 800+ page Stephen king, "11/22/63".

I also tested out the text to speech. It's a lady's voice and much, much, easier to understand than the text to speech on my kindle keyboard. It also has many speed options and I think it reads faster than my kindle keyboard version. I am very, very pleased with it.

It is much more responsive than the previous kindle fire I'm upgrading from.

If you are worried about the free offers, don't be. I DETEST commercials and advertising so much, I quit reading magazines and watching television. The offers only show on the startup, no big deal. I already took advantage of a $5.00 credit for amazon video. I was able to rent two movies and it only cost me 89 cents, when it was said and done, and I was planning on renting Hunger Games tonight, anyway. So, so far, I don't mind the offers at all.

My favorite feature is the immersion reading and the text-to-speech improvements. I also downloaded all the free kindle books with the free audiobooks for the immersion experience. These are books I always wanted to read,but never had the discipline to just read them. Reading and listening to those books are worth the price of this new gadget, IMO.

Way to go, Amazon, for a great product and a great price!

P.S.
I have an iPad, and the last time I went on vacation, I left it at home and brought only my fire and kindle keyboard. I didn't miss my iPad at all and this new gen fire is even better. Seriously, it's that good.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 2nd)

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Extender Long Range Repeater 300Mbps Router Wireless Access Point Signal Amplifier Booster Complies with 802.11n/g/b with WPS Button,Extends WiFi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices Just got this today because we are having wifi accessibility issues in our upstairs guest bedroom (and every good host knows that if you don't have decent wifi in your guest room, you can expect your guests to leave you a holy mess, in retaliation).

Couldn't believe how easy this is to set up, though! I'm pretty tech-savvy, anyhow (after 2 years of various tech-related military schools). Not that I needed to be! The included instructions are incredibly clear and easy to follow. On the contrary, the last AP/repeater I bought merely schooled me in when it's acceptable to take a hammer to one of these things. (FYI: it's right after you've tried, unsuccessfully, for an hour to get it to connect to your wifi). So I really appreciated how simple and fast this is to set up.

How fast, exactly? It literally took like 2 minutes to set up...and only THAT long because I had to go all the way into the other room and log into my laptop to complete the instructions.

Just a head's up, for the less-tech savvy:

This is NOT a wifi signal amplifier, as such. You WILL be creating a NEW wireless access point (aka wifi log-on)...even if you install this in "repeater" mode--vs. the wired-to-wireless AP (access point) mode.

So, for example, instead of logging into whatever your network is called, when you need to use the wifi that this repeats for you, you'll be logging into a new connection. They call it, by default, "My Repeater" (I assume that is so you'll never forget who actually owns it), but you can rename it to anything you want (mine is henceforth known as Fluffy Gigglebuns). You'll still use the same password as you use for your main connection, though...and therein lies the genius of it. You can make your guests feel special (or, in my case, humiliated) by personalizing the repeater network name, but the password will be the same as it is for whatever network AP you are having it repeat.

Lastly, this does offer an extra feature I think is worth mentioning:

You can also use this as a wireless adapter to connect a multimedia or other tech device that requires or ONLY allows internet connectivity via an ethernet (aka wired) connection.

So if you have something like an older roku, or game console, etc. that can only connect to the internet via an ethernet cable, you can apparently use THIS device to quickly convert it to use your wifi connection.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Extender Long Range Repeater 300Mbps Router Wireless Access Point Signal Amplifier Booster Complies with 802.11n/g/b with WPS Button,Extends WiFi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices

text_fidelity_a:
Nexus 7 from Google (7-Inch, 16 GB, Black) by ASUS (2013) Tablet This is proving to be a very nice update to the original Nexus 7. I had no problems transferring over my apps and information that I had on my original Nexus. My only quibble about the process was that it didn't duplicate the way I had arranged certain groups of apps on the screen, so I had to spend some time to recreate that.

The speakers are still located in the rear of the tablet, but are more powerful. Not a night and day difference, but audio plays clearer and louder. Still, to really enjoy a movie, you need to get an external speaker (either hardwired or bluetooth).

The overall speed is improved, including browser performance (which was already quite good on the Nexus). Other improvements include better screen resolution. It’s also slightly smaller and notable lighter. Collectively, these improvements are, for me, worth the price to upgrade.

This is a well-made all-purpose tablet. While I very much enjoy my Kindle Fires as well, the Nexus does not disappoint.

Note: be sure to update to android 4.4 when you get it. Very easy to do, and worth the time.

Belkin SoundForm Mini - Wireless Bluetooth Headphones for Kids with Built in Microphone - On-Ear Earphones for iPhone, iPad, Fire Tablet & More - Black I’m very impressed with the quality of sound from these headphones!
We got theses for our 6yo - they fit her great!
They also fit me!
The pink on these are so cute!
My daughter couldn’t wait to use them.
The ear pads are very comfortable.
The noise cancelling is very good.
I actually think that the quietest volume is a little loud. It would be nice if the volume went even quieter!
It’s nice that so much can be controlled with these headphones.
If you press the on/off quickly then it pauses/plays music or hangs up/answers a phone call.
You can even hold it down for 2 seconds to talk to Siri on an Apple device.
If you press and hold the + button then it skips the current song and goes to the next one.
If you press and hold the - button then it rewinds the current song/video - this doesn’t work on all song platforms.
I LOVE that this can be used either as Bluetooth or plugged in to an audio port.
Our iPhones don’t have an old style audio port but our iPads do. When we travel our kids get a small iPad and they can use it to watch a movie while in the car or airplane - even if their headphones didn’t get charged!!
These headphones are easy to connect.

text_fidelity_a: FiiO BTR5-384K/32Bit Native DSD256 Hi-Res CSR8675 Bluetooth5.0 Receiver/USB DAC/DSD Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced&2.5mm Balanced Output, Black) Ok, it is really Bluetooth but OMG. I own a Radsone ES100, bought it when it was the new kid on the block and it is a great piece of kit. Amazing sound, unparalleled software, so-so materials and construction. But this FiiO is like the candle you burn from both ends, you know, twice the light but half the time. This thing will drive ANY IEM’s you have to ear bleeding levels and when you look you’re at 45, OUT OF 100 on the volume scale. And while I am an IEM guy I do own a pair of HiFiMan HE-400i planars and I rarely see anything above 55 on the volume with it on Hi Gain. And granted they are only 35 ohm I have it on good authority that they will drive the big boys with out breaking a sweat. The only gripe I have is the battery life. I only run 2.5mm balanced so the battery usually taps out after about 5-6 hours. Not bad, but not the ES100’s 10 hours. But the power, man this sucker punches way above it’s weight. I use it mainly with my Samsung Galaxy phone and strictly LDAP. Everything else is disabled in the software/app that FiiO provides. And that is my second gripe. The ES100 rules on the app side. If FiiO put some time and money into providing similar functionality into their red headed stepchild app they could ask twice the price and I’d still think it was a bargain. But all the gripes aside it is definitely a step up from the ES100. Some told me if you have the Radsone that you’re good to go, no need to buy the FiiO. text_fidelity_a:
Surge Protector Power Strip with USB, Silicone Extension Cord with 10 Outlets 3 USB Charging Ports and 1 USB-C Charging Port, 1875W/15A Overload Surge Protection, Gift for Mother's Day PROS

1. It has 10 sockets/outlets.
2. Two of the sockets are offset from the other six. This allows them to be used for wide plugs, which is an important feature, because wide plugs are a frequent occurrence on appliances.
3. The color is an attractive but neutral black which makes the strip fade into the background more than the strips I own which are white or beige.
4. In addition to being a power strip, it also provides surge protection.
5. There are four USB ports that can be used for charging devices. One of them is a USB-C port and the other 3 are standard USB ports. The manufacturer claims in the manual that the three standard USB ports are “smart” USB ports.

CONS

1. I am not entirely comfortable trusting the “smart” USB ports on this device for charging. I feel more comfortable using a regular USB charging adapter and plugging it into a socket on the surge protector side of this device.

2. Regarding the smart USB ports, there are not adequate instructions either in the manual or on the manufacturer’s website that clearly explain the implications of this feature and how to utilize it. I cannot find information on the top mA it supports in charging.

GENERAL INFORMATION ON USB CHARGING

In order to test this device for my Vine review, I spent over two hours (!!!) trying to find comprehensible information on what the term “smart” means in the context of a USB port on a power strip like this one. Unfortunately, I was left with more questions than answers, for which hassle I’m dropping a star off this review. I’ve included some of what I learned below, for what it might be worth to any fellow Amazon customer who might be thinking of purchasing this product.

A smart USB charger port supposedly can, in and of itself, figure out what the optimal charging speed of a specific device is when it is plugged into that port, in order to neither overload it with too much current or under-deliver to it the optimal current. The question on everyone’s mind these days (it certainly has been on mine), is whether it is possible to destroy the battery in a particular device by slamming too much current into it. Apparently, the answer to this all-important question is: No. If, for example, you take a phone which comes with a 900mA wall charger, and you plug it into a 2,100mA charger that comes with a different device you own, it will not damage the phone. It will only speed up the length of time it takes for the phone’s battery to charge. However, if you have a USB device older than 2007, it may not charge on any USB ports newer than the (now ancient), 500mA USB 1.0 and 2.0 PC ports. Which means such older devices may not charge even on the “smart” USB ports on this device.

USB charging current is measured in mA (milliampere, 1/1000 of an ampere, the basic unit for measuring electrical current). There are three kinds of USB ports which are defined by their current specs: a standard downstream port, a charging downstream port, and a dedicated charging port. The first two are found on a desktop computer. The third kind is a “dumb” wall charger.

USB 1.0 and 2.0 standard downstream ports on a computer can deliver up to 500mA (0.5A).

USB 3.0 standard downstream ports on a computer can deliver up to 900mA (0.9A).

USB 3.1 and USB 3.2 ports can deliver between 1,500mA (1.5A) and 3,000mA (3A).

Charging downstream USB ports on a computer can deliver up to 1,500mA (1.5A).

Dedicated USB charging ports on a computer can deliver up to 3,000mA (3A).
text_fidelity_b: Surge Protector Power Strip with USB, Silicone Extension Cord with 10 Outlets 3 USB Charging Ports and 1 USB-C Charging Port, 1875W/15A Overload Surge Protection, Gift for Mother's Day

text_fidelity_a:
Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black I've said it a thousand times: "I think I could really get into (real) photography, but I just can't take another hobby that requires me carrying a whole bag of equipment across the world. If I get a DSLR, I won't take it to the places that I'd like to use it the most." Well...I think they made this camera just for me. I believe this camera to be capable of "real" pro photos, just the same as if I bought a DSLR and a single lens, which many people start by doing. It also makes a startup punk like me look like a pro, much to the chagrin of the real pros.

My other cameras include a DSC-H20, which is an older Sony model with a 10x zoom lens, multiple point-and-shoots, and a waterproof/shockproof Panasonic that I really like for my basic, worry-free shots.

My main question about this camera was, why does it appear to be Sony's flagship compact camera in every way, but yet it doesn't have the 30x optical zoom lens that some of the other Sony's have (or even the 10x of my DSC-H20)? I knew there would be an answer, but to find it, I had to start digging into camera specs, something I've been meaning to do for a while.

First, pro photographers tend to think that if you're using much zoom under most circumstances, then you're just being lazy. You need to get closer. In a landscape shot, zoom tends to flatten things out. I may have never noticed this, or WHY this is. You know, you go on vacation, take a lot of pictures, come back and some look great and others look bad. Maybe it's true that every time I zoom in on a landscape, I'm really just ruining my shot.

The other thing is aperture. Aperture basically tells you how clear the background of your picture will be versus your foreground (I'm just learning this myself, so camera pros, feel free to comment with better verbiage), a lower number being better if you want a totally clear picture, and the lowness of that number being what you use to compare the quality of lenses. It's also good to have a high end on the range because that allows you to take those artsy photos with something super clean up front and a blurry background. I've also seen some neat head shots taken that way, where even some hair starts becoming blurry.

Anyway, the low aperture on this camera is 1.8 all the way zoomed out, and 2.8 all the way zoomed in (you can set it as high as 11 in either case). This is a tight range with great numbers (notice that even here, you lose a little bit by using zoom). My camera with the 10x zoom has an aperture equal to 3.5 all the way out, similar to the 30x zoom cameras Sony has now. It makes a big difference, even to my amateur eye.

This camera, and my subsequent research, has allowed me to let go of the 10/30x zoom. Yes, those cameras are great, but this is the flagship mini for a reason. Now I understand. Just taking random pictures in my neighborhood, although so boring compared to my favorite International backgrounds, I can clearly see a quality difference.

The other main spec for cameras is shutter speed. This can be set for 1/32000 of a second all the way up to 30 seconds. The quickest shutter speeds will capture an instant in time without blur, while the slower ones will capture more action with some blur. They are also good for low light scenarios to expose the shot to more light. Very slow speeds should be used with a tripod or the camera set down someplace. This camera makes a noise (not an obnoxious one) when on auto and using a slower shutter speed, to keep you still. It's very intuitive and works well.

While you will get better shots than you ever had before using this camera on auto, the dial wheel allows you to set either aperture or shutter speed as a priority and leave the rest on auto, perfect for people that want to understand what a real camera can do, and who want to set up pro shots without yet knowing everything.

The controls on this thing are awesome. I love that there is no touchscreen to fight with and that everything is so intuitive. Great praise to Sony for knowing what fads aren't worth it. (One fad they did latch onto is that 180 degree rotating screen, which really is fantastically convenient and feels quite strong and well done). While we're talking about it, they also put in the fantastic viewfinder and the pop-up flash, which all completely recess into the body of this thing (an amazing work of engineering art).

Speaking of the flash, you won't use it often. Even on a cheap camera, I try to keep the flash off, but this thing does an amazing job of using ambient light for exposure (I believe this is the third pillar of photography). I swear, I have never seen such clear pictures in very low light. Instead of being grainy, I can pick up minute details (even zoom-able), and they appear brighter than the actual place they were taken. This, I believe, is because of the 1" image sensor they are touting. I'm impressed.

The 960fps thing. With only two seconds, this may be hard to set up the shot you want, but 2 seconds seems a lot longer in 960fps. Even just shaking your leg on camera, you'll see the odd aftereffects of your socks moving like you never did before. Stupid example, but that's the point: the details you get from 960fps slow-mo are amazing.

4k video. I really didn't care about all this until some guy at a conference pointed out how 4k has been used for pro video for years. Instead of multiple cameras to cover a hockey game, for example, you could just use one and zoom in on anything you want and still have high-def video. I realized we probably will move over to actually using it at some point. Well, here's your chance to actually use that 4k TV. It's awesome. It really is.

A note on SD cards. While most devices can read SDHC cards, which went up to 32GB, the reason they want you to have a SDXC card (which can be from 64GB to 2TB in theory) is because the speed ratings are higher. You need the speed rating of 3 (>100 Mbps) to really use these big data transfer functions. I suspect the 960fps is all that can be held in RAM, and that those speeds are way too fast for even the newest and best card (hence the 2 second limit on 960fps).

Suffice to say that I love this camera. I appreciate each of its mechanical and electrical features and how they're perfectly integrated to make this small, marvelous camera. Even in the leather case (not included), it's about the same size as my H20, certainly portable enough to have it when you want it, but with enough features and technology that you're not sacrificing anything in your photography.
text_fidelity_b: Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount This TV makes me feel bad for ever having given another product 5 stars. It is really just about perfect. Instead of wasting a lot of space talking about the quality of the picture (believe me, it is there), I am going to concentrate on some finer points, particularly those real and perceived weak points:

(This is replacing a 2009 Sony Z-Series TV, which I also love and still consider a fantastic TV; it was the first year of Internet-capable TVs if I remember correctly, and I used the DLNA features with Universal Media Server, but could never get a Plex profile to work right, so I am happy to have a newer TV that supports Plex via App, besides for the 4k, HDR, etc., etc. I have a bunch of other TVs scattered about, but the other two I use most are less expensive Samsung Smart models from five or so years ago.)

Back to (possible) negatives:

I wasn't sure I would like the stand and style. I always hated those Samsung TVs with the plastic grey legs, and I thought this would look too much like that. I thought my ideal stand was either a perfect 90-degree version of the Sony A1E, or perhaps the A8F, which I had my eye on due to its very low profile, minimalist stand. Anyway, this one looks so much better in real life than I expected. It's actually metal, and fairly dark. Placed on low furniture, it looks great walking by, and sits at the right height while watching. I guess it is made to fit a Sony sound bar perfectly (I use full surround setup, so I don't care). But I am much, much happier with the looks than I thought I would be. If that is your hesitation, go check it out in a store (before coming back for the right price).

Thickness: its thicker than some, including last year's 930E, but the way it angles out from the back gives a much sleeker appearance than you may expect just from looking at the dimensions. You only see its thickness at about 80 degrees to the side. Overall, it sits back far and takes up little extra room than it has to. The TV looks as great off as it does on.

I read a professional review that mentioned the picture doesn't look as good from a side angle. I guess that's true, but it's not nearly as drastic of a change as it sounded from the review. In fact, one of the best TV seats in my house is about 30-degrees off-center, and I don't see a difference from there at all. At 45-degrees, you start to see a difference.

Above mentioned professional review also mentioned the Android TV thing can be a little clunky. I don't feel it, to be honest. It's been nothing but good surprises for me. One thing that could be improved is customization of your home screen. You can re-order some apps, but I haven't figured out how to delete the shortcuts for stuff that isn't even downloaded. And I'm never going to play goofy games on my TV (besides real video games), so how can I get rid of that whole section that is taking up space. You can block recommended content, so after them pushing some crapware on you initially, you can basically run add-free. Looks like you'll probably have to sign in to Google, though, but you can make a new account just for your TV (which is what I do for every device).

The downward facing ports look really good with the cable management, so good that I really don't want to use any of the side inputs for permanent setups. For that reason, they should have put the IR blaster and composite input facing down as well (not that I need them, as I don't have cable, but some people will).

Not that I even checked my link speed, but manual says Ethernet port is 100mbps. Can't imagine you'll ever need more than that unless you expect to run uncompressed video without a converter.

The remote is nicer than I expected, but still not as nice as my old one. Plus, although it has Bravia Sync, it doesn't easily just control my stereo the way I would like it to (as my old Sony TV did).Not sure why there has to be a Google button on the remote. Or even Netflix. These should be programmable. Actually, four programmable Apps and/or Input buttons would be greatly appreciated in their place.

That's about it for nitpicking. Here's some things that are totally awesome (besides all the obvious):

It can read all commonly used containers for video files, including *mkv, and it can decompress 4k HEVC (H.265) video natively. So even though my NAS cannot transcode 4k on the fly, if I set it to run at full quality, the TV does it just fine! And since H.265 was made because of 4k video, here's hoping we don't have formats this TV can't play any time soon. This is just fantastic to me, as I really love my NAS' Plex server function. You can also play up to 4k H.265 video right off a hard drive via USB.

My UMS media server is showing up under Video devices (which is where the DLNA servers show up), but you can't see the files. I haven't messed with it much (because now I don't care), but I assume they'll get a profile working before long.

I love the built-in TV guide function and also the way you can browse other channels along the bottom of your screen without changing the channel. These are both great features (the TV guide function on my old TV was abandoned after a few years, but I expect this one will continue to operate). I do not have or want cable, so now I have the features that are nice to have with cable without the burden of slow response cable boxes and the burden of dealing with Comcast.

I haven't even tried out the professional settings (or even messed with anything but motionflow) because the TV is impressing me every second it's on. Again, as this is the first 4k TV to reside in my house, I guess I should be amazed. But the blacks as bars on movies wider than 16:9 are so black you don't notice them. Space scenes are to die for. 4k is done right here: this is the high end of quality, about the only thing worth removing my old Z-series for. I just love it. It looks amazing on and off, and does everything I want it to do (mainly Plex, and Netflix is nice now and then as well). I'm so happy that Plex works so well with this TV without an expensive NAS upgrade, even with movies encoded at 2160p and 7.1 surround. Just fantastic.

It's better than I expected even from Sony's almost-second-to-flagship model. About as high end as they come before they jump up drastically in price. I wouldn't have anything less on my primary TV stand, and I don't need anything more. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount

text_fidelity_a:
Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie The listing says this projector supports 1920 X 1080p resolution. It doesn't say it projects in that resolution. And it doesn't. You can see the pixel grid on the home screen. It's definitely not a 1080p projector. I don't even think it's 720p. Text is pretty blurry when you connect it to a computer as a monitor. If you do that, you might want to enlarge the font for readability.

Brightness is pretty good. It's better than mini projectors I've seen in the past. But the room (or outdoors, if you're using it there) will need to be pretty dark to get a good view. The farther away the projector is from the screen, the bigger the picture, the more spread out the light is, the darker the room will need to be to see it.

I had hopes the OS would play DVDs directly from a USB-powered outboard DVD player, but it doesn't have that functionality. I tried it and it would not recognize the connected device. You do have to manually select the input from the home screen. There are multiple inputs: HDMI, VGA, micro SD card, and USB.

The included screen is okay, but a white wall (or even ceiling) works well too.

On the bottom of the projector is a tripod mounting hole, a nice addition.

The manual keystone adjustment works only for up and down adjustment, not side to side. The focus is also manual, and works well.

The two negatives to me are that the remote control pretty much has to be aimed directly at the IR receiver ports on the projector to get it to work (there are ports on the front and back), and there is some trash inside the lens that shows up in the projected image in the one I received. I'll have to open up the projector to blow that out.

Other than that, at this price point, it's a good projector, and pretty versatile in terms of portability and input options.
text_fidelity_b: Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II Mirrorless Camera with 14-42mm II R Lens (Black) I wanted an ILM camera I could use with low f-stop manual lenses. I have some nice old f/1.9 & f/2.8 MC Rokkor lenses from 45 years ago.
My Lumix ZS70 is great for everything but low light & a few specialized uses. For those you need interchangeable lenses.
This package with two kit lenses is roughly the equivalent of my ZS70. Both lenses work fine. I'm still learning the menus & controls. It handles well on my monopod.
Edit:
I bought an inexpensive Fotasy adapter for the Minolta lenses. It works fine. The camera switches to full manual mode automatically. I did take some online advice & set up two of the programmable buttons for peaking & magnification to help with manual focusing. The resulting shutter speeds are nice, up to 8 times faster.
Edit:
This is a small camera, only a little larger than a P&S. That's normally good. Except when the temperatures are in the teens (F). Even thin leather driving gloves are a bit clumsy, especially with the back panel buttons. I normally use fingerless mittens, but not this morning.
Edit:
I'm really liking this camera. My lens changing/handling skills are coming back after not being used for [cough] years. In terms of focal lengths, the basic kit lens (14-42mm) is good for 80% of shots. I'd wish for a couple of more f-stops, though.
Edit, 5/16/2020
Longer term: Still good. I have the F3 button set on MF. There are a few cases where the AF algorithm & I disagree. For some reason, buttercup yellow flowers have no inherent contrast & AF has a hard time seeing the details to focus. This brings up peaking & magnify & allows me to fine tune the focus.
I keep wishing for a 20-80 mm f/2.8 lens. Cheap, of course. ;)
text_fidelity_b: Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II Mirrorless Camera with 14-42mm II R Lens (Black)

The maximum ports I've used at one time was 5, but it worked well. I've heard others say it gets hot, which may be true if it is full and all in use, but so far, it has worked fine for me.

Speed seems to be consistent with USB 3 ports. It actually seems to be limited by the external drives I was using. I've been trying to go through my old 2.0 backup drives to make sure they are backed up on newer drives after I lost a number of older drives recently. These drives were expectedly slower than my newer drives. I eventually want to turn my computer into something of a backup server, including videos and other large files, so this will come in really handy.

I also like that you can turn on and off the power to drives as they are needed, by pushing an on/off button for each port, or you can leave them all on if needed. Because it is powered, it does not turn off power to the ports if the computer is restarted. For my use, it is perfect.

Update 7/20/22
Running 4 external drives on it has it very hot. Makes me a little nervous. The area under it is not very hot. It is currently sitting on carpet that can handle a bit of heat. And actually the base isn't too hot, just the sides. I've been running recovery of hard drives and backups using it and it has been in pretty steady use for a few days. I don't think I would recommend this in any environment where your computer is constantly on.
text_fidelity_b: Powered USB Hub Rosonway 16 Ports 100W USB 3.0 Data Hub Aluminum USB Hub 3.0 Splitter with 12V/8.3A UL Certified Power Adapter and Individual On/Off Switches RSH-A16 (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Mighty Mule Wireless Driveway Alarm (FM231) At first I thought mine was faulty too.. we previously had a Mighty Mule driveway sensor that we loved and had for approximately two to three years before an ants nest took it over, plus damage from the weather killed it. So when that one went bad we went to Amazon to get the same model again because we loved the other one so much.. it arrived, we installed, and we kept getting faulty signals all hours of the day and night... to the point we would just unplug it at night. We attempted to call the customer service number and it was absolutely impossible to stay on hold for that length of time and not receive one person to talk to. I did the tech ticket online and did receive an email back after 2 days. That wasn't of much use. After a few tries my husband decided to turn the sensitivity down and bury the cable little bit deeper. I believe the manual says it needs to be around a foot when we only had at 6 to 7 inches..After digging a little deeper and turning the sensitivity down it seems to have done the trick. We also have an electric fence that was nearby we had to wonder if that was causing some issues? So far we've not had one faulty signal and it has alerted every time someone has come in and out of the driveway.. I would suggest before you give up and return this to try the same thing we did. The only reason it is not getting 5 stars is because you cannot get through to customer service and the tips they gave us were to no avail.
text_fidelity_b: Mighty Mule Wireless Driveway Alarm (FM231)

NIX Advance 10 Inch USB Digital Photo Frame - HD IPS Display, Auto-Rotate, Motion Sensor, Remote Control - Mix Photos and Videos in The Same Slideshow I purchased one of the 15" frames as a gift for an older relative. First the good: Once you set it up, it does what it needs to, even after a power outage. One not need to touch anything and the pictures will display on their own.

However, if you use shuffle, you'll only see a small portion of your total pictures. It seems to have favorites that it repeats over and over. There are different theories as to why this is in other reviews - all I know is it's a poorly designed feature. If you want to see ALL your pictures, you really need to never have it cycle off (which will shorten the lifespan - I got a 4 year warranty via squaretrade, so always on will work best for me).

Second, the pictures display fine, but the screen has a very bright edge. This is excessively noticeable on darker pictures or pictures that don't fill the whole screen due to the size. If you like a bright grey highlight on the outer edge of your pictures, then this is the frame for you! You can fix this a bit by playing with the brightness and contrast, but it's still an issue.

Good gift for people who need a "set it and forget it" device who may not even notice some picture defects, but if showing for your own high quality photos - especially night scenes, you will be disappointed.

text_fidelity_a:
Creative ZiiSound D3x Bluetooth Wireless Speaker I'm extremely pleased with my ZiiSound speaker. The pluses are many

Easy set up: Couldn't have been easier unless they unpacked it for me. From opening the box to streaming from my iPod touch was a matter of moments. No problem connecting at all.

Small footprint: You can see the precise measurements in the product description, but what I really like about it is how sleek/narrow it is, meaning it can fit on just about anything--a narrow shelf, a mantle, a dresser with a lot of stuff on it. While this is less of a concern in my house, I can see this being a big plus for a student in a dorm or someone in a small apartment.

Good sound: sound is crisp and clear and volume can go up surprisingly high. Bass isn't bad at all for such a small design. It's a surprisingly full sound, much better to be honest than I had expected.

Sturdy feel: it feels like it has a good heft to it and the materials feel well constructed. I assume I'll be moving it around quite a bit (I plan on using it outdoors more than anything so I no longer have to throw my speakers into a window when I sit on our patio) so it's nice to know I won't have to tiptoe around shoddy construction

Strong wireless connection: Our house is pretty small (1600 sq feet) so my connection stays pretty much wherever I am on the bottom floor. It doesn't matter what room I'm in--the walls don't have an impact. And we have a wireless network that gives it no problem at all.

Expandability: I also got the sub-woofer which really pumped up the bass in crisp, clean, room-filling fashion. I don't have any additional speakers, but I am actually considering it which comes as a bit of a surprise for a secondary system--that's how much I like this

Cons
Not fully portable: it does have to be plugged in, so you won't be tossing in a backpack and taking it to the park with you.

and um, that's about it for the cons.

In terms of sound quality, price, ease of use, size factor, expandability, there's nothing bad to say about the device and a lot of good. I'm extremely pleased with it all around, get a lot of use out of it, and imagine it as being used even more once weather turns warm again round here.

Highly recommended
text_fidelity_b: Creative ZiiSound D3x Bluetooth Wireless Speaker

SanDisk 1TB Extreme PRO Portable SSD - Up to 2000MB/s - USB-C, USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 - External Solid State Drive - SDSSDE81-1T00-G25,Black Two different units have failed for me. Google it and you'll see lots of people having issues with the 4TB version of this drive. At least for now (early 2023) this unit fails and is known to fail.

I got one from amazon, loaded it up with some data and the data became unreadable. Scrambled basically. Then the file system started failing and upon reboot the mac says it needs to be formatted. First Aid can't fix it. It's borked. Replaced it with a second unit from amazon and it had an identical probelm. Luckily for me I still had another backup. Also luckily it failed immediately. text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers With crime rates going up in NYC, this is an ideal kit for anyone living in an apartment, especially if they're alone and elderly. It covers two areas most vulnerable to thieves: your window and the door, while the key chain is best for when you're coming home late at night on a dark, lonely street. Just pull the pin and the alarm screams.

Of the three items, I would say the window alarm rates highest in terms of usefulness. In fact, I wish this set came with three of them. We travel a lot, and the biggest fear we have is intruders breaking in through our high-rise window, as we have a fire escape near one of them.

The door stop is the least useful to me as a thief would have to break through one of our windows first before going through a door. My front door is already secured by locks and the other doors in our place generally remain open. I suppose we could reinforce the front door with the doorstop, but it seems like overkill. If you lived in a dorm and wanted a particular room to be off-limits, I suppose it would be useful in that case. This item reminds me of the alarm that would be set off if you used an emergency exit. As if in acknowledgement that this item won't be used as much as the others, no battery was supplied for it, unlike the others.

As for the key chain, this is one of those devices that will lay dormant for long periods (knock on wood). You'll have to remember to check and test the batteries occasionally because it will be rarely used.

Overall, for the price this set can't be beat. It feels more like a "sampler" pack, though, as it has only one of each product when multiples of each one would have been more helpful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Kikkerland UL03-A Universal Travel Adapter, Black I ended up returning these. I'm going to France and the UK, which have different plug styles. I thought this would be a pretty cool way to get an adapter for each country in one neat little gadget. Well, it looks like it would work fine, but it's twice as big as a standard simple one-piece adapter. So, for size and weight, it works out the same as having a simple adapter for France and a simple adapter for the UK. And it's more than twice the price of two simple adapters, so for price it's worse. Independent of price, it doesn't make sense to me to have something complicated when there aren't any advantages over the simple solution. I'm concerned that the complexity just adds more ways for something to go wrong, and the last thing you want to do on a trip is add more ways for something to go wrong.

So, I don't think this product makes any sense if you just need on or two plug styles. However, you would start seeing a benefit if you need three or more different plug styles on your trip.

text_fidelity_a:
Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR This review is for the Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR.

The pros:
-Light weight for a full-sized 60-inch tripod, especially for one made of aluminum.
-Unlike some other reviewers, I really like the carrying bag. The tripod fits just fine as long as the legs are telescoped fully, and the bag seems like it is well made. It has a zippered pocket on the inside with two spare hex keys.
-Pan function is very smooth. I don't shoot video often, but I can see that this feature will be very nice for those times when I do.
-Textured rubber feet grip well, and there are metal spikes which can be revealed if needed for extra grip on ice.
-Quick-release plate is metal instead of plastic. It also can be adjusted from side to side so that it can conform to a battery hatch on the bottom of a DSLR.

Cons:
-My biggest complaint is that there is no handle to maneuver the ball head. This makes it very difficult to make fine adjustments. A removable handle, or any sort of handle for that matter, would be a massive improvement for this tripod.
-The bubble level is on the body of the tripod. It should be on the ball head where it might actually be useful.
-The release locks on the legs are absurdly stiff to open. This makes it more difficult to extend them quickly, and also makes the tripod a very poor choice for anyone with arthritic hands. I believe it will also make it quite difficult to use in cold weather with cold, stiff fingers.
-The central column is very wobbly when fully extended, and the thumb screw used to stabilize it is totally insufficient for the task.
- Edited to add: after use in the field I found that the tripod maintains a certain amount of wobble for a few seconds after handling it, or in a breeze. It's not terribly sturdy compared to similar tripods.

Overall thoughts:
This tripod seems like a good compromise for weight and price. If I wanted a lighter tripod of higher quality I would have to spend a lot more money and get a carbon fiber tripod. I do regret the lack of a handle on the ball head. While it is not terribly sturdy, and I would not rely on this tripod extended to full height with heavy glass on the camera, for casual use it seems like it will work just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR

Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema It was time to upgrade my home stereo. I've had it for decades, and I also needed a CD player. After a bunch of research, I settled on this as a solution. Moving from a full-sized receiver and larger speakers to this was actually fairly refreshing. Here are some thoughts:

Build quality
Everything felt solid when taking it out of the box. The speakers also had a nice heft. The remote felt great, too. Once I got it set up, all the buttons had a nice feel, the volume knob was smooth, and the CD tray opened/closed in a very smooth fashion. Taking a look at the back, you have all the connections you'll need for most purposes.

Sound
I was VERY impressed at how clear this thing is. It's my first "HiFi" system, and a huge improvement over the old Aiwa/Bose system that I had. When I was gearing up to buy this, I figured I might need a small subwoofer to provide a bit of low frequency support. That's not the case at all for music! These little speakers pump out rich and full sound. I may still invest in a small sub for movies, however.

CD/Bluetooth
My primary uses for this will be for music. The CD player handles all my CDs just fine (including the "enhanced" CDs that my previous players failed to play.) Connecting this to my phone was a snap, and the Bluetooth audio sounded just fine (for Bluetooth.)

Overall, this is a little powerhouse of a system, and I can't be happier.
text_fidelity_b: Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema

6. A built-in microphone allows you to use the Bluetooth function to place and received calls on your cell phone.

7. These headphones are lightweight, durable, and flexible.

CONS

1. Other than for water sports and for safety purposes, these headphones are not as good as regular earbuds, because their sound quality is comparatively quite inferior.

2. Compared to regular Bluetooth earbuds, their price is very high.

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This is a retro leather laptop messenger bag - the material is made from something called "Buffalo" leather, which feels rough and stiff - quite the opposite of lambskin or buttery soft leather. The buckles are only for show because you can open and close the bag without unbuckling it, as there are buttons underneath. It has a weathered look, with varying shades of brown and sienna that give the impression that you're an Indiana Jones-type adventurer who's been carrying this bag through the outback, escaped tigers and bears, and came through fine, though the bag is a bit battered.

In other words, it's very manly, and harks back to the 1940s when bulky items were the norm because thinner materials hadn't been invented yet. While it looks great and seems well made (it's from India), it's actually limited in terms of actual everyday use. If you're traveling a lot, you want things to be as lightweight as possible. This is not one of those items. Even when empty, it feels cumbersome to carry. Stuffed with a laptop and papers, it will be heavy.

Think about it - when was the last time you actually saw someone on the train or airport carrying one of these? You might say you'd like to do so because it will make you look unique. In reality, other people may have tried carrying one of these and gave up.

So while it's nice as a conversation piece and something you might want to show off to your friends, I fear it will be one of those novelty items that, after its newness has worn off, will be relegated to the back of the closet.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

CozyPhones Sleep Headphones - Over Ear Headphones from Ultra Thin Cool Mesh Wired for Side Sleepers, Meditation, Running, Laptop, and Phone - Pink Lycra This sleep headphone band fits quite comfortably. Before I bought this I was introduced to the product at my mom's house and I wear a considerably bigger hat size than her, but the stretchy band fit both of us perfectly. Despite my big bobblehead of a noggin, I don't find this too tight even when worn for hours, and yet it hasn't become stretched out either. A smaller headed person could still wear mine. Also in regard to fit, the light weight, low profile speakers can easily be moved inside the headband to exactly where they are most comfortable and best heard for each wearer (I did have to move the speakers back when I tried my mom's). Once in place the speakers stay put really well simply due to the friction between the textures of the fuzzy fabric pad over each speaker and the headband's fabric. I occasionally have to tweak where a speaker is sitting as I put them on, but once in place the speaker has never needed to be repositioned during wear. I also love that the speakers can be slipped out through the back so the headband can be laundered.

I would say that the sound quality is that of average headphones. I don't notice a discernable difference between these and any other headphones I own, but I may not have as attuned an ear as some people seem to have, so my feelings won't be hurt if you get a second opinion on this part.

I don't really have any cons to mention for these, but wait, I almost forgot to mention that when buying these I saw multiple other reviewers warn that the dye bled from the colored edge of their headbands. I should say that I specifically bought the one with the white edge to avoid that happening. I've had no dye transfer at all from mine, so I can suggest getting the white edged band if that's a concern.

Hope this helps.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV 65" Omni Series 4K UHD smart TV with Dolby Vision, hands-free with Alexa When I saw this 55" TV on Prime Day sale for $299, hands-free with Alexa, and with no-interest payments over 24 months, I just jumped on it. I've spent almost that much over time replacing lost remotes! I didn't realize how big this TV is, so I almost cancelled the order...but I'm glad I didn't. I've got it sitting on one of those sturdier metal and plastic folding tables (like a card table but rectangular), and I've plugged my Mac Mini into one of the HDMI ports so I can also use it as a computer monitor. What a difference! I can have all kinds of things I need at any given time open and placed around on the screen (see photo), and because I work in my recliner that's a good distance from the TV, I can read everything very well and get to all my open windows super-fast. Then, at night, when I'm ready to watch TV, I can sit back on the daybed that's on the opposite wall and watch it all on the big screen.

My 2014 LG soundbar works with it, but it's only got the optical port cable and cannot be controlled with Alexa. One of the Fire TV tech guys very patiently told me what I need to get if I want to upgrade my sound setup, and I went on and ordered one of the Echo Dots on sale for 19.99 because I couldn't find the one I bought before. I'll probably get a new soundbar at some point but, for now, I can certainly watch TV and listen to music using the one I have. But right now, I have to have the remote to control things that Alexa cannot control, and I keep it in a remote wrangler tied to my daybed (where I also sleep). I thought at first that the TV was just turning itself on by itself in the middle of the night, but then I realized that either I or one of my dogs was flopping over onto the remote, turning it on. That's a temporary issue because once I have an Alexa-compatible sound system set up for it, I can hang the remote on the wall and forget about it.

I've read a number of reviews of the Fire Omni TV series, and they are shown to be on the lower end, picture-wise. If I had wanted a super-duper knock-your-socks-off viewing experience for MSNBC, which is what I watch more than anything else on the TV, I would have to have spent five times as much, and why would anyone do that? Well, if you're really into the primo video experience and have the bucks, I guess you might...but this TV is perfect for me. The #1 selling point for me, other than the rock-bottom sale price, is the fact that I can control pretty much everything with my voice.

I did knock off a star for one reason and one reason only: In the Inputs setup, you can specify what type of product you have on a particular HDMI port. Soundbar, gaming console, etc., but there is no selection for "Computer." I want to be able to say "Alexa, open my computer." Now I have to say "Alexa, open H D M I 1." Cumbersome. I hope Amazon will add the Computer input with a future software update.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV 65" Omni Series 4K UHD smart TV with Dolby Vision, hands-free with Alexa

Instead, this backpack has quite a few well-done features, and the overall appearance is very striking.

It’s made mostly of canvas, which gives is a “broken in” look right from the start. It’s a very nice change from the usual nylon packs. The canvas is thick and sturdy, and has a great feel to it.

The build quality is impressive considering the price. The stitching is all tight and even, the zippers are of good quality, and the snaps/fasteners are all solid and durable. The strap padding is a little thin, but still comfortable. I was really pleased to see that there was padding on the back. That’s not an option I was expecting at this price. It gives the pack a much more comfortable feel when it’s loaded down.

The inside is lined with a smooth, snag-free lining that’s either nylon or poly (not 100% sure). In any case, it is also very well stitched, with no loose threads, sags or puckers in the material. It makes it very easy to slide books, laptops, etc. in and out of the pack. There are also a couple of compartments inside the pack, both zippered and open, to help organize all the little items that everyone needs to tote around. Additional pouches are on the outside of the pack, which are great for easy access. I didn't have any problem stowing all my small items inside of some type of pouch.

The size is ample for a typical laptop plus a few other items. I loaded it down with books to see if it could take the weight, and the pack performed very well.

The build quality, looks and performance make this an excellent value for the price. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a pack that won’t break the bank in terms of cost.

Gosky 12x55 High Definition Monocular Telescope and Quick Smartphone Holder - 2018 This is a really nice optical device. I hadn't necessarily heard of Gosky before, but I gather they are a big brand in optics. I'm also going on relatively little education on the subject that a monocular is easier to focus at longer distances and/or a larger range of distances because you don't have to focus the two lenses - something which makes it hard for me to look through binoculars after a while.

This is pretty lightweight, but feels very solid and nice. It has a turn-out piece to the rear of the rear lens to accommodate people who don't wear glasses. And besides that, there is only one knob to turn to focus, mostly depending on the distance to the object of your attention.

The carry case is fairly rugged nylon and has a belt loop, but not the kind of belt loop you can use without unstrapping your belt. It's also a little large for a belt in my opinion, but may come in handy. The hand strap is pretty nice, but there is a lot of extra length to the strap I really don't know what to do with, and I feel like the actual attachment process could be more refined. I do really like that both lens covers can stay attached to the body while not in use (rear one can be attached to the hand strap and front on is attached to a rubber ring which stays on the body) which makes for a refined and complete product.

Not sure if this one can accommodate a cell phone holder or not...seems like people must take pictures through these things when birding or spying or watching opera or whatever they're doing.

Nice product. I now have a good feeling about this brand that was previously off my radar.
text_fidelity_b: Gosky 12x55 High Definition Monocular Telescope and Quick Smartphone Holder - 2018

text_fidelity_a:
Echo (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa, (RED) edition What a disappointment. Bought this for my son for Xmas, and it was a COMPLETE FAILURE.

First of all, this thing takes FOREVER to boot (we're talking like 5 minutes. Not even kidding.). That's insane. It was a complete PITA to set up (kept hanging and needed to be reset and configured again and again), and then, after all that, despite saying it was successfully set up, it NEVER WORKED. Gave nothing but errors.

I'm even pretty tech savvy, and have automated my entire house by myself, so this should have been easy-peasy, right? If this device wasnt a piece of junk, I imagine it would have been.

For example, despite being told it was successfully set up, when I tried to test it by asking it to play a certain song that I often play on other Alexa-enabled devices , it would announce the name of the song and artist, then go, "Sorry. Something went wrong."

Just to be sure it wasn't on Alexa's end or a problem with my Amazon Music premium account, I went to all the other Echos and dots in our house and asked them to play the same song. Each did with ZERO problems.

So I thought, "Maybe it just needs to be updated." So I told Alexa to update, and she responds, "Sorry, I'm not programmed to do that now, but I'm always learning. Try again some other time."

I googled Echo updates and found that Echos are supposed to be auto-updatable as soon as they are connected to wifi, and this one WAS connected to wifi, so this was complete B.S.

I reset the Echo, tried again, it said it successfully set up (again) and, again, it failed to carry out ANY commands. I contacted Amazon Help and waited for a response. I reset, then unplugged, the Echo time after time, waited for 15 minutes, then tried to set it up again. Over and over. Every single time it said the set up was successful. And every single time it failed to do ANYTHING I told it to do.

Worth noting: when I googled the problem, there was site after site and thread after thread of people complaining about the same, or very similar, issues, from as far back as a couple years ago and right up until the day I went through all this. Even Amazon's own Alexa pages came up all over the search.

So, CLEARLY, Amazon is very much aware of these issues and, yet, they still continue to sell these defective Echos anyhow.
text_fidelity_b: Echo (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa, (RED) edition

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling I've had the opportunity to review three different G.G. Martinsen players, and of the three this one is my favorite. I brought two of the players, pre-charged, to review at my sister's where I am staying a week while she had and recovers from surgery, and the one thing I can say right off the bat is that I wish the charging cable was of the ubiquitous Micro-A type and not the mini type, which I did not think to bring with me. The [[ASIN:B016F4AGLC other player]] handles like the [[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ first one]] I reviewed for G.G. Martinsen, but I will have to wait until I get back home to do anything other than test the recorder and FM radio on this 16GB player because I have no cable to copy music onto the player with!

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports Disclaimer: I was sent this product to evaluate so that I could write an informed review.

Actually this is my second LotFancy cooling pad, and I took it because I do like their products. I haven't had any bad experiences with them except for breaking off one of the little plastic stops that keeps your laptop from sliding off the pad when the rear is elevated, but that was entirely my fault. I left the pad on the floor and someone stepped on it. Can't blame LotFancy for that.

The design of this pad is kind of interesting. It has two controls, one for the large center fan and the other for the four smaller side fans. This, plus the width of the pad itself, allows you to use various sizes of laptop efficiently. If you have a small one, you never need to turn on the side fans. If you have a 17" one, they're in position to help you cool it. I'm curious as to why the green light (signaling that the center fan is on) is set so much lower than the light for the side banks. A strange feature, though not something I have a problem with. It's just odd.

The pad is adjustable to seven different heights (including flat), so you've got a lot of positions to choose from. I write in a variety of places around the house, so this is one of my favorite things about the pad. It allows me to work without having to find all sorts of things to prop my laptop on. The locking mechanism is solid. Since it's USB-powered, there's an extra USB port at the back so that you don't lose that functionality. Most cooling pads have some way of doing this, so it's expected rather than special. It's quiet, but it's far from super silent.

It's a good pad. Yes, some of the construction seems a bit flimsy, but my other LotFancy pad has held together just fine and I see no reason to think this one won't.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer I've had a love/hate relationship with Harmony for the past 10 years...but no more second chances.

Just like every Harmony I've ever owned, setup for this required a call to tech support. I'm fairly tech savvy, and this should be easy to set up, but it wasn't. And I know it wasn't me because it took tech support 30+ minutes and 7 syncs to make it function "properly". Yes, "properly" is in quotes because even at its best, it was unimpressive.

On my own using the software, syncing failed to load my activities into the remote. And again...it took tech support 7 syncs to make it work.

Even after it was working "properly", it was still frustrating to use:

1) When switching between TV and SMART TV, it would power the speaker bar on and off. Does Logitech not understand that TV and SMART TV are not 2 separate devices and if you are switching from one to the other the sound should be left on? With a remote this expensive I shouldn't have to dig out the speaker bar remote to turn it back on every time I switch activities.

2) Lack of physical buttons for numbers is annoying. Any time I need the number pad I have to swipe to unlock, then swipe to get to the number pad. Technology is supposed to make processes faster...not slower. And yes, I know I can turn off the lock feature...but then every time I grab the remote it does something I don't want, and that something usually requires time-consuming troubleshooting.

3) As I mentioned before, programming this remote is a nightmare (2+ hours) and even then it couldn't stand alone. I ran into problems only tech support could solve, and even then it took 30 minutes AFTER I had all the correct devices loaded. Please note that this was a simple configuration: Sony smart TV/Fios DVR/Samsung speaker bar. All less than 3 years old. After I returned this remote I bought a "learning" remote and endured programming every single button individually, and it still took a fraction of the time.

4) There is no POWER button. Only an OFF button. You turn things on by selecting an activity. And as stated before...switching to a new activity powers things off that a remote this expensive should understand should be left on. If you are going to have a single OFF button that powers down everything with an activity button that turns everything back on, you should have an ON button for each device so you can quickly turn on any device that for whatever reason doesn't turn on when you fire up the system with an ACTIVITY button. And again...having to do an initial swipe to get to the ACTIVITIES just to turn the system on is annoying. Why does Logitech insist on writing code that slows down the power-on process???

5) You cannot utilize the Harmony software without plugging in the device. Why??? When things aren't working correctly (which is often) we should be able to fire up the app just to review the settings. Then, when you do plug the remote in, you have to wait for the remote and your PC to establish communication. Don't software engineers understand that we HATE waiting for technology to do things? Especially when forced to plug in when we don't want to??? Speaking of plugging in, it is difficult with this remote. First off, there is a totally unnecessary door. That door gets in the way when you're trying to plug in, and plugging in is difficult enough already because the mini-USB port is deeply recessed inside the door. Do we really need to cause all this hassle just to hide a mini-USB port? C'mon Logitech...don't you guys own cell phones? Mini-USB doors are annoying and useless (which is why cell phones stopped using them). Try to keep up.

6) Tech support is only good for 90 days. Based on my experience with this remote and 2 previous Harmony remotes, this means that any changes I make to my very simple home entertainment system will not work, and I will not be able to get help to make them work.

A remote that costs well over $100 should assimilate my entertainment system like the Borg. It should be simple to set up, function extremely quickly/efficiently, and be highly intuitive. This device is just another example of technology that steals away hours of your your life that you will never get back.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer I've had the Harmony One remote since the day it came out, and now "upgraded" to the Harmony Ultimate Remote.

Build and Setup:
This is a very solid remote. It is heavy for its size with clean lines and elegant design. Inside the box is the powered hub with two remote blasters, remote, base, and power cords for the hub and the base. There does not appear to be a removable battery like with the Harmony One.

Set up was very simple. As I already had my settings in myremotesetup.com, I simply had to log into myharmony.com, transfer my settings to the new remote and the remote was setup. It was very easy.

The difference between this remote and other Harmony remotes is that this has a hub and blaster units that connects through your wireless network to allow you to connect and control your units with your smartphone.

You have to connect the hub and blaster units around the units you want to control. It has to be connected to your home wireless network, which was easy. You can either do it through myharmony.com or by pressing the setup button on the hub and your router (if it supports it) it was that easy.

I have my hub on the shelf with my Blu Ray, Dish Box, and Xbox. The one blaster is near the television, and the other is on another shelf with my Wii and my surround sound box. When you go into advanced settings on your remote you tell the remote to control the devices with either just the remote, with the hub, blaster 1, blaster 2, or all of them. This allows flexibility where you setup and place your devices and blaster and hub units.

Using the Remote:
The remote is easy to use. Many of the major buttons; play, pause, fast forward, volume and such are hard buttons on the remote. The remote has a large touch screen that can do all the other device options you may seem fit to try. It scrolls across several pages: Home screen allows you to choose between actions such as watch tv or dvd, channel favorites (which you program), current action screen that controls actions related to what you are doing, and finally the number screen, here is where you can enter numbers to change channels. This last part is a bit of a pain as when I am channel surfing I like to be able to press number buttons to change channels and you really can't do this with this remote without looking.

To operate DVR like functions you can also swipe up from any screen to access a black screen where you can program gestures. By default you press to pause, swipe right to skip forward, swipe right to swipe back, etc.

Phone App:
The phone app for the android is a bit lacking as it is not quite as sophisticated as the remote itself, but can do most of the actions of the remote as long as you are connected to the same wireless network as your hub is.

Troubleshooting:
The remote is easy to use and troubleshoot, Simply rebooting or re-syncing the remote can resolve most problems I've found. It also prompts you for assistance the first time you add an action or new device.

Overall this is a great remote. This will demand, though, some knowledge on your part as it is a very sophisticated remote. Many problems that occur can easily be resolved by some knowledge of networks, remotes, or Harmony devices in general. If you have experience with this you will enjoy the functions and capacity of this remote.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

Accsoon CineEye Video Transmitter, 5G Wireless Live Transmission to 4 Devices, 1080p WiFi HDMI, 100 Meter Range, Supports Android & iOS, RGB, 3D LUT Loading, Incredibly Low Latency – Grey (CineEye) This is a great solution for a remote monitor for video shoots, and it's simple, no wires, no cables, and basically one-button operation. You install the app on your device (iOS or Android), connect the transmitter to your video camera (via HDMI), boot it up, then connect your device to it via WiFi. Launch the app and you're looking live at the video camera output. It delivers 1080p at 60fps and pushes audio to your device too. It's actually pretty awesome.

We gave it a real test in a room full of servers and a lot of potential electronic interference and it delivered a solid signal and connection up to about thirty feet. Beyond that it dropped a frame every now and then, but not bad.

If you're recording video through the app on your device, there's ten-minute limit per file, something to do with restrictions on the app's classification. That doesn't interfere with the camera recording video. It's just a file recording limit on whatever device you're monitoring the video on, if you choose to capture it while you view it.

The build quality is great. It feels practically indestructible. Battery life is solid.

If there is one thing to complain about, it's that the Android app is a bit blah. The iOS version is a lot better.
text_fidelity_b: Accsoon CineEye Video Transmitter, 5G Wireless Live Transmission to 4 Devices, 1080p WiFi HDMI, 100 Meter Range, Supports Android & iOS, RGB, 3D LUT Loading, Incredibly Low Latency – Grey (CineEye)

It provides a significant upgrade on the pseudo-4k projector with an impressive 2600 lumens making it one of the brightest projectors out there easily surpassing the 1500 lumens you would get with the entry level Sony true 4K projector. One of the big upgrades is the move to 18Gbps bandwidth giving you the ability to do 4K at 60Hz. Note that you do need to have a wired connection to get the full 18Gbps -- you only get 12 if you do the wireless option that the 5050ube offers over the regular 5050ub. Even with the reduced bandwidth that you get with the wireless setup, it is a great convenience to have the ability to stream from sources without having to run a wire from the source to the actual projector.

Another great aspect of the 5050 is the motorized lens which is a feature that other more expensive true-4k projectors do not offer. Of course with Epson you do get exceptional HDR quality as well as amazing black.

This is an impressive pseudo-4K projector that provides features that are not even found in some entry level true 4K projectors. If you are not absolutely dying to get true 4k, then this should be one of the projectors you should consider.
text_fidelity_b: Epson Home Cinema 5050UB 4K PRO-UHD 3-Chip Projector with HDR,White

Emergency Radio 4000 mAh, Hand Crank Radio,Solar Weather Radio, Portable AM/FM/NOAA Weather Radio with Bright Flashlight&Motion Sensor Reading Lamp,SOS Alarm, Phone Charger for Hurricane,Survival This thing does exactly what it sets out to do. It's a versatile tool that is good to have in a pinch. The lights work great. The reading light is incredibly light and can be used as a lantern. The difference between the front COB is a wide dispersed patterned compared to the focused beam of the center LED. The combo of the two adds a good bit of forward brightness so you can get good front and periphery lighting.
I think I initially would have liked a digital tuner, but at the end of the day, I've not seen a digital tuner have the ability to fine tune like a knob. The sound from the speaker is crystal clear and loud.
The hand crank works okay. I received this radio with at least 75% power indicated by the three blue leds. I cranked it for a bit and all 4 leds were lit. The handle is a little on the small side and isn't all that comfortable to grip, but it does work well.
I didn't get the motion sensor to work. I really doesn't know what it does.
Overall, it's a great multi purpose device to have in case of emergency. And while it doesn't include a ham radio, it can recharge the batteries on my ham so I can send out communication. So having a renewable power source is a nice bonus.
text_fidelity_b: Emergency Radio 4000 mAh, Hand Crank Radio,Solar Weather Radio, Portable AM/FM/NOAA Weather Radio with Bright Flashlight&Motion Sensor Reading Lamp,SOS Alarm, Phone Charger for Hurricane,Survival
