The description says it does not come with an SD card or AAA batteries, but mine did, perhaps for review purposes, although the box did not look like it had been opened. Seems like it would come with that stuff, so perhaps other reviewers might clarify. There is a case and two separate pouches for the wider camera lens and the microphone.

Functionality and video quality are pretty good. I guess the only drawback is that this almost seems like a throwback now. For still pictures - on a vacation or a great hike where I want to take great pictures - I still take along a small camera instead of just my cell phone, but the truth is cell phone cameras are getting so good now that I wonder when that will no longer seem prudent. And with that said, my small camera takes such amazing (not studio quality) HD that I wonder when something like this would really seem like the best thing, especially considering they both take SD cards and length is only limited by SD card capacity.

It certainly does seem like a more professional camera in its size and shape, but mostly because that style has been the trend for some time now. But in a way this style is already starting to seem outdated, like a throwback. I also noticed, just now, that even the really big name manufacturers have this style in 1080p for comparable prices.

I'd definitely give this thing a look. I would have totally loved it a few years ago. The mic and extra lens still feel like premium features, but I'm rarely the one to set up for photos and video footage, as I usually just do landscapes or great spontaneous moments. This may be a fantastic alternative to giving kids your phone - or a phone - to play with. Seems like a good way to encourage their inner photographer without it leading into a bunch of cheap phone games.

Camera has mini* USB and HDMI ports (as opposed to micro) - just when I was wondering what I'd ever do with this one mini-HDMI cable I have... Mic takes 2xCR2032 batteries, which are included, and should probably last, as I don't think mics eat up much power. Has a curled, springy, analogue audio cable with stereo mini-plugs on both ends to connect the mic. Also has an external battery charger.

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Slate, Small/Large If you hate the thought of wasting money on something that will just end up falling off your wrist, then DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. I purchased two Fitbit Flex models, one for myself and one for my husband, on April 30, 2015. I didn't buy them from Amazon, but I did buy them from an authorized retailer. By October, my husband had quit wearing his because it wouldn't sync (we figured out this was easily fixed by restarting the phone the Fitbit app was installed on). He put his up and I continued wearing mine. During this time, my Fitbit started unlatching and falling off my wrist occasionally. I would find it laying around, or would notice, then retrace my steps and find the tracker. Fast forward to January: my Fitbit tracker fell off and was lost for good. I couldn't find it anywhere. I assume some lucky soul found it and calls it their own now. I started wearing my husband's tracker at this time with no issues. Then in March, it fell off my wrist in the parking lot of my office. I didn't notice this until it was too late. Someone I work with found it and returned it to me. Unfortunately, it was ran over by a vehicle (judging by the marks on the band) and crushed. No more Fitbit. Full disclosure: I tended to play with the fastener on my first Fitbit, though I made myself not do that anymore after losing it and using the second one. I also had 9 total bands with which I used the Fitbits in  this review. I though rotating between the bands daily would keep the fastenings tighter and reduce the risk of losing my Fitbit. Not so. When I decided to contact Fitbit and ask if they might be able to help me remain a loyal customer by giving me a percentage off my next Fitbit purchase, they obliged after a string of emails back and forth, sending me an email code to be used ONLY on their website. The discount was for 25% off, which is the everyday price on many of their items on Amazon. I should have pushed for more, but I didn't realize that until I went to compare their web prices with those on Amazon. In short, I feel like I dropped $200+ on Fitbit products and all of that money was lost. Their products with a watchband type fastener seem to be better, so my only caveat is that if you choose to buy the Flex, be prepared to lose it. I am currently without a tracker and have thought about buying one, but I am gun shy when it comes to dropping another $150 on a Fitbit Charge HR (has a watchband fastener) when I know the company doesn't stand behind their products. Sorry, Fitbit.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Slate, Small/Large

This feature is important to me, because not all my music is properly tagged, so music organizing software like itunes doesn't recognise the files. text_fidelity_a:
LeeKooLuu Backup Camera Rear View Monitor Kit HD 1080P for Car Truck Minivan Waterproof Night Vision DIY Grid Lines LK3 The camera and kit are a superb value. Installation was not difficult (including BOTH TIMES, I had to install the cable). Let me explain: When ordering it doesn't tell you what size cable comes with it, which is a 23 ft. cable. I found this out the hard and dirty way after a couple of hours on a winter Sunday afternoon painstakingly dragging myself underneath my truck; routing, securing, and cable-tying the camera cable from the back of my 2009 Ram 1500 (crew cab short bed) to the front, just to find out when I went to bring it through the firewall, I was about 5-7ft too short to reach the middle of my trucks console and mounting location. Pretty frustrating after spending hours to install and come up short. On re-reading the instructions by LKL they advised 'if cable too short, contact us for the longer 33ft. or 50ft cable'. Uhm OK, and I sent an email, and to their credit, they responded within a couple of hours asking for the size I wanted that would work. Unfortunately, a "short splicer" cable wasn't an option with both male finish end couplers on their cables to simply "Splice" into what was already routed 95% of the way already, so I asked for the 33ft. one. They sent it immediately, and I got it a few days later with plans to complete installation the following weekend from my original effort. So, new cable in hand I had to re-route the new cable basically starting over. A bit frustrating BUT hopefully this post will change their ordering system to ask "cable size" based upon application upfront; like for a car. SUV, truck, or RV. If, not simply message them ahead of time to install to see if they can send you a longer cable. not as efficient, but will save you the double-install time.

That said, I really like my camera. It has great clarity, good screen size, and detail. I like the flexible options for 16:9 vs. Narrower field, grid options and adjustments, etc. I also recommend adding LED back up lights to improve the night view of the camera which already includes some LEDs to help with night safety (you are likely reading this because you want better safety, and rearview vision, especially at night, correct?) You will already be removing one taillight assembly installing the splice-in to power the camera with the backup light wire, so you might as well install LED Backup bulbs both sides of the taillamp assembly.

I had a perfect spot in mind to install my camera in the center on top of my dash above the radio into a little "coin tray" recess. I had to snip about a half-inch off the camera holder base front and back to make it nestle in the bottom and adhere with the provided mounting tap securely. If I had it to do over again I likely would get their wireless camera product first, then see if the wireless signal worked OK given the length of the truck. (They don't recommend their wireless version for larger vehicles, like full-sized SUV's, trucks, or RV's but reviewers have reported satisfactory results with trucks and SUVs) Although it's a bit more $$ for wireless the amount of install time required for do-it-yourselfer's, or professional installation would be well worth it. If the wireless signal isn't good enough, return it since it wouldn't have been installed fully; then just order up this wired option. Good luck and happy backing up!
text_fidelity_b: LeeKooLuu Backup Camera Rear View Monitor Kit HD 1080P for Car Truck Minivan Waterproof Night Vision DIY Grid Lines LK3

text_fidelity_a:
Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001 I've had this enclosure for almost 2 years. My five year old computer was very slow and I was having lots of trouble with it and the enclosure connecting to it. I did get it to connect and do one backup, but that was it. So, I thought surely it was my pc that was the problem. It would either not connect or it would not do anything...like I didn't have it plugged in. I just thought all three connections had to be made properly for it to come on and do it's job. I am not completely tech stupid, nor savvy.
I am disabled, so I was saving for a new computer. I have had lots of sickness over this time, and getting to this was not a huge priority and I never came back to read reviews. I wish I had.
I finally did recently get a new pc, and just the other day wanted to give it another go. When I plugged it in, again, there seemed to be no power... and then suddenly there was a burning smell and smoke coming from the enclosure where the power supply went in. It was quite scary, because I almost did not catch it soon enough.
I took a long shot and contacted the company anyways, even though it had been such a while to explain the long ordeal, and why I had not contacted sooner... Among my sickness, I was giving the device the benefit of the doubt, because I honestly thought it was my pc.
This is the message I received in return "In this case, it is highly commended to stop using this hard drive enclosure.
According to your information, this item is faulty. Regarding our products, a 12-month warranty is provided, however, it is obviously that the item ordered on 2016 has been far beyond its warranty. Hope that you could understand."
They did offer a 15% "return after purchase" discount refund if I would purchase a new one. But, as I am disabled, I cannot afford to do that at this time.
Hopefully, my backup really is on the hard drive that this unit supposedly saved it to that one time, as some beloved photos of my deceased father are on there, and I don't have them anywhere else.
I wish I were more tech savvy and didn't stay sick so much... Even so, I wouldn't have known the problem until I got a new pc anyways. Based on my experience and other reviews, I would not recommend this enclosure to anyone.
I do hope this helps someone.
text_fidelity_b: Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001

text_fidelity_a:
Headphone for Men This is a great idea: the combination of a USB 3.0 hub and a gigabit adapter. It's a perfect space-saving option -- the overall size is just a bit larger than my gigabit adapter and I get 3 USB 3.0 ports as a bonus!

The build quality is very good. It seems odd to use the word "stylish" to describe such a device, but this is quite stylish -- the case is black with a steel gray brushed top (which looks like metal, but I believe it is plastic). The case is sturdy and has tight seams, and the USB and RJ45 ports are well-anchored. The connection cable is short (about one foot long) but very stout with an well-made USB connector on the PC end.

Setup is quick and easy. The hub portion is a straight plus-and-play install on Win 7 (and, I would imagine, other Windows versions as well). The Ethernet adapter requires drivers, which are supplied on an included CD-ROM (which I'm pleased to report is a full-size CD rather than those mini ones which are such a pain to use).

The hub is passive (no external power) so there are limitations as to what it can support. I didn't have any problems using it with low power draws, such as thumb drives.

It comes with a brief, but well-written user guide.

Well-made, works great, and a easy, compact way to add two different functions to a laptop (or any other PC). Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Headphone for Men

text_fidelity_a:
Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver I'm an amateur radio operator and generally use headphones, especially when trying to understand weak signals. I wanted something to give my aging ears a bit more volume when I need t. I also wanted to be able to share what I was listening to with visitors using additional headphones.

I found the HA400 to serve both purposes admirably. I put it into 24 hours of continuous service just after receiving it. It worked beautifully in boosting the volume when needed it. In addition, visitors found it useful to be able to adjust their individual headphone volumes.

I haven't actually measured the dynamic range of the HA400 yet, but this past weekend's experience makes me believe it is excellent within the boundaries of the levels that come out of the headphone jack of my receiver. I noticed no distortion during operation.

I believe the HA400 is a good choice cost-effective choice for amplifying and splitting a single audio stream into four headphone-level stereo channels.

Be aware that it requires 1/4" stereo plugs to mate with. You will need adapters if you have cords with 1/8" plugs. The unit comes with a wall wart power supply with a generous length of output cable. There is no ON/OFF switch.

FWIW, I'll be ordering one or two more HA400s for use with our home entertainment equipment. I ordered this unit from Amazon on another account, hence no "Verified Purchase" notation. The price was competitive and delivery reasonable.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver
